title: Composition plan
description: One plate's renderer-neutral information design (AES-V2.16b / SUE-628). It sits between the article and any renderer: the semantic plan says what relationships must survive, the composition plan says what geometry carries them, and the renderer route says who is allowed to draw what. Rules here are derived from benchmarks/EDITORIAL-INFOGRAPHIC-INFORMATION-DESIGN.md and are enforced against the failure signatures in evals/negative-baselines/SUE-570-INFOGRAPHIC-FORENSICS.md. Nothing in this file names a renderer.

artifact_profile.description: Which of the pinned visual families this plate is. Only the information-design families are in scope for SUE-628; thumbnail and concept-illustration are deliberately absent.

article_ref.description: Which article this plate serves. Lineage, not content.

renderer_route.description: deterministic: a program emits the whole plate. hybrid: a program owns all factual layout and text, a non-deterministic step contributes bounded non-load-bearing material. generative_support: a generative renderer contributes atmosphere only and never owns factual layout, exact text, labels or relation geometry. Plain `generative` is deliberately not representable for these three families.

generative_support.description: Required when renderer_route is hybrid or generative_support. Enumerates what the non-deterministic step may contribute. Everything not listed stays deterministic.

load_bearing.description: Must be false. A generative contribution that is load-bearing is a routing error, not a style choice.

semantic_plan.description: What must survive into the reader's head. Renderer-neutral.

primary_question.description: Exactly one. A plate that answers two questions is two plates (SUENGJ-ARTICLE-IMAGE-FAMILIES.md section 6; signature F4).

modules.description: 2-4 load-bearing modules. The ceiling is derived, not stylistic: roughly 3-4 typographic tiers are distinguishable at a ~14px mobile floor, so a fifth simultaneous module either collapses the tiers or demands a size differential too small to perceive (trait T10).

relations.description: At least one. A plate with modules but no relations is a list.

reading_order.description: Module ids in the order the reader should encounter them. Must be a permutation of modules[].id — a partial order means the path forks, which is a split trigger.

must_preserve.description: Information that may not be dropped by any downstream compression. Minimalism that deletes these is semantic deletion (SUENGJ-INFOGRAPHIC-CALIBRATION.md section 5).

evidence_boundary.description: Trait T11: the observed/asserted boundary is made visible by medium, not by a device inside the artwork. The plate demonstrates; the caption asserts.

information_gain.description: Trait T14. Prose is inherently sequential; a plate earns its place by producing something a linear medium structurally cannot. This is the operational form of the VISUAL-INFORMATION-GAIN.md gate.

label.description: A short stable semantic label. Never a mutable article/section title, date, caption or citation (signature F6).

role.description: observation: the article states it. interpretation: the author claims it. open_question: the article leaves it unresolved.

carries.description: What this module contributes to the plate BEYOND its own text — the quantity, structure or position it renders. A module whose only content is a sentence in a box is signature F3 and must be rejected or merged.

prose_only.description: Declared true when the module carries no geometry. Always invalid; the field exists so the defect is representable and therefore testable rather than silently unrepresentable.

type.description: The relation vocabulary from benchmarks/EDITORIAL-INFOGRAPHIC-INFORMATION-DESIGN.md section 2. The relationship is named BEFORE the geometry is chosen (trait T2) — this is the layer the chart lane inherited and the infographic lane never had.

basis.description: stated: the article says it. interpreted: the author infers it. Carried into the caption layer, not stamped inside the artwork.

magnitude_channel.description: Trait T7: when magnitude is shown, it rides a continuously-scaling geometric attribute, not discrete buckets or a legend key.

dimension.description: The comparison dimension this relation is about. A comparison plate genuinely carries several correspondences between the SAME two modules — one per row — and trait T4 makes each row's delta load-bearing, so collapsing them into one relation loses information the plate exists to show. Required to be distinct when two relations share the same from/to pair, so a repeated pairing is a real set of rows rather than a duplicate.

composition.description: What geometry carries the semantic plan. Still renderer-neutral: this says what position means, not which library draws it.

reading_order_mechanism.description: Trait T3: reading order comes from geometry. Arrows are the fallback for relationships that are genuinely non-spatial, not the default. Module lettering is not an option — it is what a plate does when its geometry cannot say what the order is.

enclosure_budget.description: Trait T10 / contradiction C2. Typography carries structure through size, weight, case and asymmetric whitespace for roughly 3-4 tiers. Enclosure is necessary only where the structure is NOT hierarchical — independent parallel categories with no rank relation, where size and weight have no 'which is bigger' answer. Everything else drawn as a box is a tier typography could have carried.

typography_roles.description: At most four. The available type-only channels are size, weight, case and asymmetric whitespace; past 3-4 distinguishable tiers the prescription is to split the content, not to invent a fifth tier (trait T10).

connector_channels.description: Trait T5. Containment, flow and authority need three distinct visual channels; authority is the one most often collapsed into flow, which forces captions to disambiguate what the geometry should carry. Required whenever the plate carries a containment or authority relation.

max_labels.description: Checked against the artifact profile's text_policy.label_count_ceiling. The ceiling existed before and nothing enforced it (signature F7).

stable_only.description: Must be true. Mutable article/section titles, dates, captions and citations belong to the caption layer, not the artwork (signature F6).

annotation_strategy.description: Trait T6: a qualifier fuses to the relationship it qualifies rather than being externalised to a legend the reader will not consult.

mobile_strategy.description: Trait T9 / signature F5. Professional practice renegotiates height and holds type size, re-stacks, swaps in a plate built for the surface, or splits. Uniform downscaling is not among them and is deliberately not representable in this enum.

min_type_px.description: Effective rendered type size at viewport_px, not the authored size. The SUE-570 set rendered 5.2-8.7px here.

downgrade_disclosed.description: Contradiction C3: a true matrix cannot serialise into a list without losing the joint-condition read. If one axis is collapsed on mobile, the downgrade is disclosed rather than hidden.

geometry.description: Trait T1 and signature F1. Spatial position must encode exactly one declared thing across the whole plate, and which thing must be a decision rather than a residue. Position encoding NOTHING is legitimate and honest for a topological plate; position encoding nothing while LOOKING like it encodes something is the failure.

position_convention.description: scale: an axis carries a measured value. controlled_comparison: position carries which variable was varied. containment: position carries nesting. topological: position carries nothing and the plate says so.

x_axis_encodes.description: Name the axis. Null only when the convention is topological or containment. The acceptance test is literal: if neither dimension can be given a semantic name, the plate is a list wearing a diagram's clothes.

time_scale.description: Trait T8. Required when any relation is temporal. proportional when the gaps carry meaning the reader needs; ordinal when only order matters. Ordinal applied to duration-critical data fails silently, which makes it the more dangerous direction for an automated system.
